instructions: Apply the following repository policy checks in addition to normal code review. Inspect the complete headers of added and modified files even when the header is outside the diff hunk. Review the MR/PR title and description against the complete diff once per review, and report description findings in the review summary rather than on an unrelated code line. Give concrete evidence and a suggested correction for each finding. If the title, description, or required file context is unavailable, state that the corresponding check could not be completed rather than assuming it passed.

rules.rule: Check added and modified project-owned source files, headers, scripts, and build files for license notices consistent with LICENSE.md and the established headers in comparable project files. This project uses Apache-2.0: require the SPDX-FileCopyrightText notice and SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0, with comment syntax appropriate to the file type. Accept correct SPDX-only headers, as used by existing project files; absence of the full Apache 2.0 boilerplate alone is not a finding. Preserve existing valid boilerplate and follow comparable project files when choosing the header form for new files. Flag missing, contradictory, or altered license terms and identifiers, including leftover incompatible notices. Compare license changes with the target branch; do not treat a license edited in the MR itself as automatic authorization to relicense files. Preserve legitimate third-party licenses, attribution, and documented exceptions; do not demand that third-party code be relicensed. Do not require comment headers in formats that cannot contain comments, binary/generated assets, or documentation where the project does not use such headers. Limit findings to reviewed files.

For every added or modified project-owned file that carries or should carry a copyright header under project conventions, require its project copyright notice to include the applicable year YYYY. Use an explicit current review date supplied in the review context; if unavailable, use the year of the MR/PR head commit's committer date supplied in that context as the contribution-year fallback, not as proof of the current calendar year. Do not infer dates from training data or neighboring headers. If neither date is available, report that this check could not be completed. Preserve the original first year and copyright holder. A single older year N becomes N-YYYY, an older range N-M becomes N-YYYY, and a notice already including YYYY is correct. A genuinely new file uses YYYY alone; a renamed, moved, or copied existing file retains its original first year and includes YYYY. Preserve third-party notices and valid multi-year notices; never shorten a range or remove a later year to match the fallback. Flag missing or stale project dates even when the header was not edited. Do not request year updates in untouched or deleted files, unmodified third-party notices, generated files, or binary assets.

Treat the MR/PR title and description as the future squash commit subject and body. Require a concise, specific title in imperative mood, as required by CONTRIBUTING.md, and a self-contained description explaining what changed, why it changed, and the resulting behavior or impact, in proportion to the change. Compare them with the final diff: flag missing material changes, inaccurate or stale claims, vague summaries such as 'misc fixes', placeholders, and descriptions understandable only by following external links or reading review history. Prefer a short paragraph or a few focused bullets; flag redundant detail, raw logs, local machine paths, and review conversation history that obscure the change. Retain required project template sections, issue references, and relevant test checklist entries; do not demand an arbitrary word count or unnecessary implementation detail. Flag validation claims only when they demonstrably contradict the available diff or CI evidence. Missing evidence alone is not a contradiction: do not infer which checks were or were not run when the description is silent, and do not reject regression checks merely because they cover behavior outside the diff. Report one consolidated description finding with a concise proposed rewrite grounded in the diff, without inventing motivation or test results.
